sentence: If it rains tomorrow, I will ___ at home.
taskText: If it rains tomorrow, I will ___ at home.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. If it rains tomorrow, I will ___ at home.
explanation: 'Will' takes the base form 'stay' to describe the plan for tomorrow.

rationales.staying: After will, use stay, not the -ing form.
rationales.stay: 'Will' takes the base form 'stay' to describe the plan for tomorrow.
rationales.stays: Do not add '-s' to a verb after 'will'.

sentence: You can sit here if the seat ___ free.
taskText: You can sit here if the seat ___ free.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. You can sit here if the seat ___ free.
explanation: The seat is singular, so the condition uses 'is free'.

rationales.be: The seat needs a present-tense verb; use 'is', not 'be'.
rationales.are: 'Are' goes with plural subjects or 'you', not the seat.
rationales.is: The seat is singular, so the condition uses 'is free'.
rationales.am: Am goes with I, not the seat.

sentence: If you need help, ___ me.
taskText: If you need help, ___ me.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. If you need help, ___ me.
explanation: 'Call' is the base verb used to give the instruction after the condition.

rationales.calls: A direct instruction uses call, without -s.
rationales.calling: Calling alone cannot give this instruction.
rationales.to call: An instruction begins with call, not to call.
rationales.call: 'Call' is the base verb used to give the instruction after the condition.

sentence: 'If you are hungry, there is bread in the kitchen.' When is the bread useful to you?
setupText: Choose the meaning of the message.
taskText: 'If you are hungry, there is bread in the kitchen.' When is the bread useful to you?
text: Choose the meaning of the message. 'If you are hungry, there is bread in the kitchen.' When is the bread useful to you?
explanation: 'Hungry' means wanting food; the speaker tells you where to find some.

'Hungry' means wanting food; the speaker tells you where to find some.
Wanting sleep means being tired, not hungry.
The message offers food, not help finding a place.
A shower is for washing; hungry describes needing food.

sentence: If the bus is late, we ___ walk to work.
taskText: If the bus is late, we ___ walk to work.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. If the bus is late, we ___ walk to work.
explanation: Can walk gives an available choice when the bus is late.

rationales.can: Can walk gives an available choice when the bus is late.
rationales.are can: Do not put 'are' before 'can'; 'can' is already the helping verb.

sentence: If you ___ cold, close the window.
taskText: If you ___ cold, close the window.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. If you ___ cold, close the window.
explanation: 'You' takes 'are': 'if you are cold'.

rationales.am: Am belongs with I, not you.
rationales.be: Use 'are' as the present-tense verb after 'you'.

sentence: If the shop is closed, ___ wait outside.
taskText: If the shop is closed, ___ wait outside.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. If the shop is closed, ___ wait outside.
explanation: Don't wait is the negative instruction for the situation in the if-clause.

rationales.not: A negative instruction needs don't before wait.
rationales.doesn't: Doesn't describes a third-person action; it does not form this instruction.
rationales.no: No cannot directly make wait into a negative instruction.
rationales.don't: Don't wait is the negative instruction for the situation in the if-clause.

sentence: 'If you are free tonight, come for dinner.'
setupText: Choose the meaning of the condition in this invitation.
taskText: 'If you are free tonight, come for dinner.'
text: Choose the meaning of the condition in this invitation. 'If you are free tonight, come for dinner.'
explanation: Here being free means not being busy; the invitation depends on that.

rationales.Because you are free: Because gives a reason and treats being free as a fact; if leaves it open.
rationales.On the days you work: Working is not the condition in this invitation.
rationales.When you are not busy: Here being free means not being busy; the invitation depends on that.
rationales.After you eat dinner: Tonight is the time, but eating dinner first is not the condition.

sentence: If my phone ___, please answer it.
taskText: If my phone ___, please answer it.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. If my phone ___, please answer it.
focusKey: coverage-conditionals-a1-849:Third-person present verb in a condition
explanation: 'My phone' takes 'rings' in this present-tense condition.

rationales.ring: 'My phone' is singular, so add '-s' in the present simple.
rationales.rings: 'My phone' takes 'rings' in this present-tense condition.
rationales.ringing: 'Ringing' needs a helping verb; it cannot stand here alone.
rationales.to ring: To ring is not a complete verb for the subject my phone.

sentence: 'If the bag is heavy, ask me for help.' The bag is heavy. What do you say?
setupText: Choose the reply that follows the instruction.
taskText: 'If the bag is heavy, ask me for help.' The bag is heavy. What do you say?
text: Choose the reply that follows the instruction. 'If the bag is heavy, ask me for help.' The bag is heavy. What do you say?
explanation: The instruction says to ask for help when the bag is heavy.

rationales.Can you help me?: The instruction says to ask for help when the bag is heavy.
rationales.Where did you buy it?: Asking where the bag came from does not request help carrying it.
rationales.Is the bag new?: The bag's age is not the condition given.
rationales.What color is it?: Asking about color does not follow the instruction to request help.

sentence: Take this umbrella if you ___ one.
taskText: Take this umbrella if you ___ one.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. Take this umbrella if you ___ one.
explanation: You need completes the condition; one refers to an umbrella.

rationales.needs: After 'you', the present-simple verb is 'need', without '-s'.
rationales.needing: Needing alone does not complete the condition.
rationales.to need: 'To need' cannot serve as the complete verb after 'you'.
rationales.need: You need completes the condition; one refers to an umbrella.

sentence: 'If the light is green, you can enter.' The light is green. What does the message say?
setupText: Choose the meaning that matches the message.
taskText: 'If the light is green, you can enter.' The light is green. What does the message say?
text: Choose the meaning that matches the message. 'If the light is green, you can enter.' The light is green. What does the message say?
options: You can turn off the light.
focusKey: coverage-conditionals-a1-852:Recognizing permission when a condition is met
explanation: The green-light condition is true, so the message permits entry.

The message gives permission to enter, not to use the light switch.
The green-light condition is true, so the message permits entry.
Waiting outside does not match the permission to enter when the light is green.

sentence: If there ___ two cups, we can have tea together.
taskText: If there ___ two cups, we can have tea together.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. If there ___ two cups, we can have tea together.
focusKey: coverage-conditionals-a1-853:There are with a plural noun
explanation: There are introduces more than one cup.

rationales.have: There have does not introduce the existence of the cups; use there are.
rationales.are: There are introduces more than one cup.
rationales.be: This condition needs the present-tense form are, not be.

sentence: I'll make coffee if you ___ tea.
taskText: I'll make coffee if you ___ tea.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. I'll make coffee if you ___ tea.
explanation: "You don't want" uses "don't" plus the base verb to make a negative condition.

rationales.don't want: "You don't want" uses "don't" plus the base verb to make a negative condition.
rationales.doesn't want: With you, use don't, not doesn't.
rationales.not want: Add "don't" before 'want' to form this negative present-tense clause.

sentence: 'If you are tired, sit down. If you are thirsty, have some water.' You are thirsty.
setupText: Choose the instruction that matches the situation.
taskText: 'If you are tired, sit down. If you are thirsty, have some water.' You are thirsty.
text: Choose the instruction that matches the situation. 'If you are tired, sit down. If you are thirsty, have some water.' You are thirsty.
explanation: 'Thirsty' means needing a drink, so the water instruction applies.

Sitting down is the instruction for being tired, not thirsty.
Opening the door is not an instruction in this message.
'Thirsty' means needing a drink, so the water instruction applies.
The message gives no instruction about a light.

sentence: If Sam ___ at work, call his home number.
taskText: If Sam ___ at work, call his home number.
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. If Sam ___ at work, call his home number.
focusKey: coverage-conditionals-a1-856:Negative be with a singular subject
explanation: Isn't means is not and agrees with the singular subject Sam.

rationales.doesn't is: Do not use doesn't with is; negate is directly.
rationales.aren't: Sam is one person, so use isn't, not aren't.
rationales.isn't: Isn't means is not and agrees with the singular subject Sam.

sentence: 'If the room is hot, open the door.'
setupText: Choose the words that give the condition.
taskText: 'If the room is hot, open the door.'
text: Choose the words that give the condition. 'If the room is hot, open the door.'
focusKey: coverage-conditionals-a1-857:Identifying the condition rather than the response
explanation: The words after if describe the situation that makes the instruction useful.

The words after if describe the situation that makes the instruction useful.
'Open the door' is the action to take, not the condition.
'Hot' describes the room in the message, not the door.
The message does not say the room is open.

sentence: Can I use your chair if you ___ need it?
taskText: Can I use your chair if you ___ need it?
text: Choose the grammatically correct completion. Can I use your chair if you ___ need it?
focusKey: coverage-conditionals-a1-858:Condition attached to a permission question
explanation: You don't need forms the negative condition in this request.

rationales.doesn't: Doesn't goes with he, she or it, not you.
rationales.don't: You don't need forms the negative condition in this request.
rationales.isn't: "Isn't" cannot be followed directly by the base verb 'need' here.
rationales.not: You need don't, not just not, to make this present-simple negative.

sentence: 'What will you do if the cafe is closed?'
setupText: Choose the reply that matches the question.
taskText: 'What will you do if the cafe is closed?'
text: Choose the reply that matches the question. 'What will you do if the cafe is closed?'
options: The cafe is on King Street.
explanation: I'll go answers what you will do when the stated condition applies.

This gives closing time, not your plan if it is closed.
This gives a location, not an action you will take.
I'll go answers what you will do when the stated condition applies.
This describes a drink; it does not answer the question about your plan.

sentence: ___ I have time on Saturday, I'll visit you.
setupText: Choose the completion that means the visit is possible, but not decided.
taskText: ___ I have time on Saturday, I'll visit you.
text: Choose the completion that means the visit is possible, but not decided. ___ I have time on Saturday, I'll visit you.
explanation: If leaves having time open and makes the visit depend on it.

rationales.Because: Because presents having time as a reason, rather than an open condition.
rationales.Before: Before puts the visit earlier than having time; it does not express this condition.
rationales.So: 'So' introduces a result and does not connect these clauses in the intended way.
rationales.If: If leaves having time open and makes the visit depend on it.
